rationale: The /flags call is made with v=2 (flags_service.py params v='2'), which returns a dict per flag, so the bool/str/else branches cannot fire. Same defect as the thread on the unreachable non-dict branches.

person_id really is an unvalidated CharField, so a malformed UUID reaches the ORM and raises Django ValidationError; but it does not escape - the broad `except Exception` at 3412-3414 turns it into a generic 500. Real gap (should be a 400), mechanism misstated.
The sibling `versions` action maps VersionNotFound to 404 and VersionHistoryIncomplete to 422 (feature_flag.py:2470-2478); the new path collapses both to 400. Real contract inconsistency.
Self-dismissed non-finding: rollout_percentage arrives as an exact JSON number, so `== 0.0` is fine. Nothing for a reviewer to act on.
`distinct_ids[0]` with no ordering guarantee; bucketing is distinct-id-sensitive. Identical to the thread on unstable distinct_id selection.

The in-memory FeatureFlag copies only name/active/deleted/version/filters, so bucketing_identifier, evaluation_runtime, ensure_experience_continuity fall back to model defaults and are shipped as the override. Same defect as the thread.
rollout_excluded is gated on is_zero_rollout in every branch, so exclusion by any 0<pct<100 rollout is never reported. Same as the thread.
`matched: all_properties_matched` contradicts the serializer help_text 'Whether this condition was the one that matched' (feature_flag.py:1970). Same defect as the thread.

updated_at is auto_now=True, which Django forces to editable=False, and model_to_dict skips non-editable fields, so the key can never be present. Dead branch (created_at, default=timezone.now, is editable and does fire).

OperatorType is serde(rename_all='snake_case') (property_models.rs:4-6) but the analysis emits format!('{:?}').to_lowercase(), producing 'noticontains'/'isdateafter' instead of 'not_icontains'/'is_date_after' on the wire.

PropertyAnalysis.value is a JSONField without allow_null while Rust emits Value::Null for is_set/is_not_set filters (types.rs:640, property_models.rs comment). Outbound is_valid(raise_exception=True) then fails and the blanket except returns 500.
return_debug_info was deleted from the signature but posthog/api/person.py:1443-1449 still passes return_debug_info=True, so that (debug-only) branch now raises TypeError.
`except Exception: raise` is a no-op left behind after the contextual wrapping was removed. Same as the thread.

analytics_dashboards is not in the exclude list; ManyToManyField.value_from_object returns Dashboard instances when pk is set (Django related.py:2035), so any flag with an analytics dashboard makes the override payload unserializable and the request 500s.
The f-prefixes are indeed placeholder-free, but F541 is explicitly ignored repo-wide (pyproject.toml:310, '~1139 existing'), so there is no lint or behavior consequence.
The new tests mix datetime.now(UTC) with created_at-relative offsets and retro-fitted ActivityLog timestamps; a wall-clock dependency in version-boundary tests is a real if minor flake risk.
person_existed_at_timestamp is imported inside the method while its two module siblings are imported at feature_flag.py:88-91. Same as the thread.

FlagsResponse carries errorsWhileComputingFlags and quotaLimited and FlagDetails carries `failed` (types.rs:198-212, 395-407); the endpoint reads only `enabled`, so an errored or quota-limited evaluation is returned to the caller as result=false.

Every other 500 path in this file calls capture_exception (560, 2354, 2399, 3154, 3413); the three new failure paths (3456-3461, 3502-3507, 3612-3614) only log, so these errors never reach the exception tracker.

AutoField does not set editable=False (django/db/models/fields/__init__.py AutoFieldMixin sets only blank=True), so model_to_dict does include `id`. The asserted 'every override fails to parse' does not hold.
Self-ruled-out non-finding about ReDoS from caller-supplied regex; no action for a reviewer.
`auth_token == *internal_token` is a byte-by-byte String comparison of a shared secret. Same point as the thread's constant-time suggestion.

build_condition_analysis iterates only filters.groups; super_groups, feature_enrollment and holdout (flag_models.rs FlagFilters) also decide the outcome, so the analysis can show every condition matching while the flag is off with no explanation.

The only matching index is ['team_id','scope','item_id'] (activity_log.py:136-137); the new query adds created_at__lte plus ORDER BY -created_at, so rows must be sorted. Accurate, modest, and the index shape is pre-existing.

The new `|| self.only_use_override_person_properties` short-circuit skips prepare_flag_evaluation_state entirely, which is what loads cohorts, static cohort ids and group type mappings (flag_matching.rs:1997-2045) - so cohort/group conditions mis-evaluate on the historical path.
Self-downgraded observation that the tests mirror internals; no actionable defect stated.
No test file references test_evaluation anywhere in the tree. Same as the thread demanding tests before merge.
PropertyType is written as crate::properties::property_models::PropertyType four times while OperatorType from the same module is imported at types.rs:6. Cosmetic but correct.
A production DRF action named test_evaluation becomes the public route /test_evaluation; a naming concern only, no functional effect.

match_property is called with the person-property map for every filter regardless of prop_type, so cohort, group and flag-dependency filters are looked up in person properties and reported as unmatched with a fabricated explanation.
The comment says 'prioritize person_id over distinct_id' while 3430 prefers the caller-supplied distinct_id (and the serializer forbids both). Comment contradicts code.
person_existed_at_timestamp has no test anywhere and gates a user-visible 400; the thread's minimum-coverage list names exactly that case ('Person exists but didn't exist at timestamp -> 400').
`assert first_update_time < between_updates_time < second_update_time` compares created_at+10m, +15m and +20m, so it can never fail. A no-op assertion.

version_history.py:18-21 validates timezone-awareness while point_in_time_properties silently calls timestamp.astimezone(UTC) (which assumes local time for a naive value) and lost its isinstance guard. Real inconsistency, low practical impact via DRF.

match_property returns Err for In/NotIn and FlagEvaluatesTo (property_matching.rs:425-432); unwrap_or(false) turns those into matched=false with a wrong explanation instead of surfacing 'inconclusive'.
required_scopes=['feature_flag:read'] on an action that returns the full person_properties blob. Same as the thread proposing person:read or filtering.
The siblings use LocalEvaluationThrottle and RemoteConfigThrottle, both subclasses of BurstRateThrottle (feature_flag.py:410-414, 432-435); ClickHouseBurstRateThrottle is not used here.
person_existed_at_timestamp hardcodes max_execution_time=10 while build_person_properties_at_time threads the caller's timeout (PIT:182). Correct, minor.
flat=False is values_list's default and the sibling query at VH:121 omits it. Redundant argument.

FEATURE_FLAGS_SERVICE_URL defaults to http://localhost:3001 (settings/data_stores.py:535) and nothing requires TLS, so the new bearer secret can cross a plaintext hop. Accurate, but this is the established in-cluster pattern.
Self-ruled-out: the existence query uses %(name)s parameter binding, so there is no injection. Non-finding.
Self-dismissed: /flags takes the team token in the body, so the Authorization header is not otherwise occupied. Non-finding.

One global INTERNAL_REQUEST_TOKEN (config.rs:609-611) now gates arbitrary flag-definition override, detailed analysis and the billing skip, with no per-team binding, expiry or rotation path. A design point a reviewer should see.

get_person_properties (flag_matching.rs:1692-1717) has no fallible path - it returns Ok unconditionally - so .ok() discards nothing, and the None fallback reports condition-level match, not 'every property unmatched'.
Self-ruled-out: all reconstruction queries use bound parameters. Non-finding.

When no versioned entry is found and timestamp < updated_at the function returns 1 unconditionally; if the activity log was trimmed or the flag never had a v1 entry, reconstruct_flag_at_version(1) then treats current state as the creation state and returns silently wrong history.

Every Rust test touched by the diff just sets detailed_analysis/only_use_override_person_properties to false and passes None for the override arg, so no test exercises the new behavior or the internal gate - the thread's point about the gate being untested.

The comment claims .iterator() avoids loading all entries into memory, but `entries_list = list(entries)` at VH:235 materializes up to MAX_HISTORY_ENTRIES (10k) rows anyway. Code contradicts its own comment.

log_activity returns None without saving when activity=='updated' and changes is empty (activity_log.py:818-826), so the 'entry without version info' the test claims to create never exists and the test asserts nothing.

The isinstance(timestamp, datetime) guard was removed, but test_point_in_time_properties.py:38-41 asserts ValueError('timestamp must be a datetime object'); that existing test now fails (a str would raise AttributeError later instead).
The parameterized case 'current_version' supplies timedelta(hours=1) but the body branches on _name and substitutes datetime.now(UTC), discarding the parameter. Test smell.
Self-ruled-out: `flags` is the request-local Vec taken from flag_result, so the mutation cannot poison the shared cache. Non-finding.

detailed_analysis is gated in mod.rs:218-222 but only_use_override_person_properties is forwarded raw from the query string, and skip_writes ORs both - so any public caller can suppress experience-continuity writes with ?only_use_override_person_properties=true.
A parse failure or a key that matches no flag only logs a warning and evaluation proceeds against the live definition, so a historical request silently gets present-day results instead of an error.
The diff deletes an unrelated blank line before check_rollout; pure noise in an otherwise scoped change.
An explicit 'could not verify' note about deprecate_field inside model_to_dict; no claim a reviewer can act on (django_deprecate_fields is not vendored here either).
Self-dismissed as correct: both new params reuse deserialize_optional_bool like their siblings. Non-finding.

One `except Exception` wraps ~100 lines including the outbound is_valid(raise_exception=True) at 3608-3609, so response-shape bugs and HTTP errors from the flags service are all flattened into 'Failed to evaluate flag'.
get_person_properties clones and re-merges the property map for every flag when detailed_analysis is on. Real, but the detailed path is a single-flag internal debug call, so the cost is negligible.

The slice is applied to a newest-first ordering and the loop keeps the last versioned entry in chronological order, so truncating older rows cannot change the version returned; the asserted corruption mechanism does not hold.
Self-dismissed as bounded; no action.

The block is documented as unreachable (comment at 1094-1095) and the new isinstance check raises ValueError into an except (ValueError, TypeError) that float() already triggered, so the added lines change no outcome.
Self-dismissed: the same decorator order is used by the sibling actions at 3343-3353. Non-finding.

Accurate that the read is not audited, but no read path in this viewset (or the equivalent person point-in-time endpoint) writes an activity entry; this is an org-wide policy question, not something this PR changed.

The distinct_ids used for the historical property replay are the person's current (post-merge) set, so ids merged in after `timestamp` contribute $set events that did not belong to this person at that time.
`headers = {}` is untyped while the adjacent `params: dict[str, str]` carries an annotation. Cosmetic.

The replay matches event='$set'/'$set_once' or JSONHas(properties,'$set') - it never checks JSONHas(properties,'$set_once'), so $set_once carried on an $identify event is dropped, and non-event property sources (API/import updates) are invisible.
logging.exception(f'...{e}') uses the root logger and an f-string interpolated exception while the module logger is used everywhere else. Same as the thread.
Up to four tracing::info! lines per override entry, two dumping full FlagFilters Debug output. Same as the thread asking for debug/trace.
is_internal_request has six branches and no #[cfg(test)] module, and the billing skip and override loop are equally untested. Same as the thread.

internal_request_token=os.getenv('INTERNAL_REQUEST_TOKEN') with no settings entry and no validation is the same dependency the thread flags: if it is unset the Rust side silently drops detailed_analysis and returns empty analysis.
In/NotIn return Err(ValidationError) from match_property, and the caller's unwrap_or(false) makes that false - the operator cannot 'flip to match' on an absent property.
Self-dismissed as unreachable scale; condition counts cannot approach i32 overflow.
`*flag = override_flag` replaces key, id and team_id with caller-supplied values and nothing validates identity. Same defect as the thread (and its duplicate).
AGENTS.md:134 states 'Python tests: do not add doc comments'; several new tests carry docstrings. Correct convention violation, cosmetic.

The comment calls it 'the efficient single-pass method' while reconstruct_flag_at_timestamp runs find_version_at_timestamp then reconstruct_flag_at_version - two activity-log queries (version_history.py:280-287).
No lower time bound, no LIMIT, full properties blob via toJSONString and a double json.loads. Exactly the thread's blocking finding.

Cross-tenant reach was correctly ruled out: the flag list is fetched for the authenticated team and the matcher uses self.team_id for cohorts, groups and person lookups, so a forged team_id in the override does not read another tenant's data.

The only sibling that returns a reconstructed dict does it with Serializer(instance=result).data (feature_flag.py:2481); validating an outbound payload with data=+is_valid is unique here and is what turns a shape mismatch into a 500.
The new docstrings use a Google-style 'Raises:' block while the pre-existing function in the same module documents exceptions in prose (VH:88-89). Cosmetic inconsistency.

Existence is 'any event at or before the timestamp' while properties come only from $set-bearing events, so a person with events but no property events passes the gate and then evaluates against an empty property dict - a silently wrong historical answer rather than the 400.
Self-dismissed: skip_serializing_if keeps the field absent for existing clients. Non-finding.

A second unbounded events scan with no event filter, run before the property query. The thread makes the same point ('person_existed_at_timestamp a few lines up is a redundant round trip').
Self-dismissed and correct: FlagEvaluationReason has no rename_all, so condition_index and conditions are exactly the keys Python reads. Non-finding.
Serialization failure sets override_definitions=None and the historical request proceeds against the current definition. Same defect as the thread.
The new POST declares no throttle_classes while local_evaluation (3049) and remote_config (3624) both do. The thread names this explicitly as the DoS half of its finding.
Only flag_result['conditions'] matches the Rust FlagDetails contract; the other three or-branches cannot fire and would mask a future shape change. Same as the thread.
ORDER BY timestamp ASC with no tiebreaker over a last-write-wins fold: events sharing a timestamp can be applied in either order, so the same query can return different properties across calls.
Self-dismissed and pre-existing (module-level RECONSTRUCTABLE_FIELDS is untouched by this diff).
get_distinct_ids_for_person_identifier has no callers left anywhere in the tree yet keeps its signature updated by this diff. Dead but harmless.

The internal-request early return emits no counter or log, so requests that skip billing are invisible. Accurate, but it mirrors the adjacent skip_writes guard, so the gap is pre-existing in shape.
